content_html:
Everything you need to know before your adventure

Why travel to Peru?

Peru is one of the most fascinating destinations in the world: It combines ancient history, spectacular natural landscapes and world-renowned cuisine. From the magical Machu Picchu to the Amazon jungle, Peru has something for every type of traveler.

What is the best time to travel?

  • Dry season (April to October): Ideal for visiting the mountains (Cusco, Arequipa, Puno).
  • Rainy season (November to March): Greener, fewer tourists. Perfect for the jungle.
  • Popular dates:
    • Inti Raymi (June)
    • Holy Week (April)
    • National Holidays (July)

What documents do you need to enter?

  • Valid passport (minimum 6 months).
  • Visa: Not needed for most countries in America and Europe for tourism (up to 90 days).
  • travel insurance: Recommended, not required.
  • COVID-19 vaccination certificate: Currently not mandatory, but subject to change.

What is the approximate budget?

How to move within Peru?

  • Internal flights: Recommended for long distances (Lima–Cusco, Arequipa, etc.).
  • tourist buses: Comfortable, safe and cheap (Cruz del Sur, Oltursa).
  • Taxis or apps: Uber, InDriver or safe taxis in cities.

Unmissable places to visit

  1. Cusco and Machu Picchu
  2. Sacred Valley of the Incas
  3. Arequipa and the Colca Canyon
  4. Lake Titicaca and Puno
  5. Peruvian Amazon (Puerto Maldonado or Iquitos)
  6. Lima (gastronomy, history and sea)

What to eat in Peru

  • Ceviche
  • Lomo saltado
  • Chicken chili
  • Lima cause
  • Quinoa and Andean superfoods

Useful tips for the traveler

  • Always carry cash, especially outside of Lima and Cusco.
  • In Cusco, acclimatize 1–2 days because of the height.
  • Use sunscreen: even in high-altitude cities it is very sunny.
  • Learn basic words in Spanish: they will help you connect better.
